# Excellence 2026: Connected Communities Solutions in Action


October 29, 2026


by Craig Patton


##


Government works best when information can move with the people and processes that depend on it. But disconnected systems, manual handoffs, and departmental silos can slow that movement, create duplicate work, and make it harder for public-sector employees to see the full picture.


Connecting technology across workflows can change that. When systems and data work together, organizations can improve coordination, give employees timely access to information, and create more seamless services across departments, agencies, and the communities they serve.


## Celebrating Excellence in Connected Communities Solutions


The[Tyler Excellence Awards](https://www.tylertech.com/about-us/tyler-client-difference/tyler-excellence-awards) recognize organizations putting those connections into practice. As 2026 winds down, we’re highlighting this year’s Connected Communities winners — organizations integrating Tyler solutions to break down silos, connect workflows, and help people work together more effectively.


## Connecting Information for Safer Jail Operations


Recognizing the strains of manual and duplicate data entry between law enforcement and jail operations, the[Caddo Parish Sheriff’s Office in Louisiana](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/caddo-parish-restores-control-and-command-with-a-safer-jms) adopted an integrated public safety environment. By connecting arrest and booking workflows, the Parish:


- Reduced data entry for booking staff
- Processed more bookings in less time, allowing increased patrol time
- Increased staff awareness and safety with accurate data during required booking checkpoints


“Redundant data entry is gone,” said Robert Montoya, security captain. “Arrest data arrives before the inmate. Records are instantly available across classification, records, and jail staff. That alone saves time across stakeholders.”


## Building a Connected Justice Ecosystem


With limited integrations and manual workflows across courts and law enforcement,[Hidalgo County, Texas](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/hidalgo-county-the-upgrade-that-built-a-justice-ecosystem) , modernized its technology stack in a multi-phase upgrade that transformed access to justice. The county has:


- Integrated public safety and judicial systems through a modern, scalable platform, increasing transparency and public access
- Reduced back-and-forth paperwork between courts and law enforcement
- Decreased manual data entry of traffic and criminal non-traffic citations


“Processes that used to take hours or days now take minutes,” said Clarissa Longoria, senior IT manager. “None of this would have happened without the upgrade.”
